matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission logic bug: using && instead of || in the team admin/owner check, incorrectly requiring both roles and blocking valid admins/owners.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email comparison defeats the blacklist check and duplicate attendee filter (emails not lowercased before comparing), allowing blacklist bypass via mixed-case emails and duplicate attendees differing only in case
Duplicate emails within a single request are never rejected server-side — the uniqueness refinement only exists in the client-side schema, so direct API calls can insert duplicate attendee rows

`sendAddGuestsEmails` is passed the raw input `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees in the input to receive the wrong email template (AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by removing emails already present in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted). However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw input `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the template selection depends on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`: matching emails get `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, non-matching get `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Therefore, if the user includes an existing attendee email in the input along with new ones, that existing attendee will be incorrectly treated as a “new guest” and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` rather than the intended `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email sending failures are swallowed with a bare `console.log` that doesn't even log the error object, leaving guests persisted but never notified and showing the user a success toast

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` which swallows all failures and does not log `err`. The handler has already persisted new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(...)` and then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless of email send outcome. On the client, `AddGuestsDialog` shows a success toast in `onSuccess` and closes the dialog, so the user is told guests were added even if notifications were never sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic operation: DB write, calendar update, and email sending are separate steps — if the calendar update fails after the DB write, retries fail with uniqueness errors and the calendar stays permanently out of sync with the DB

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the flow is: (1) update DB via prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...) then (2) await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) (no try/catch) then (3) sendAddGuestsEmails in a try/catch. If step (2) throws after the DB write, the mutation fails but the DB has already been changed. A retry will compute uniqueGuests by filtering out emails already present in booking.attendees; because the previous attempt inserted them, uniqueGuests becomes empty and the handler throws BAD_REQUEST ("emails_must_be_unique_valid"), preventing the calendar update from ever being retried via this endpoint. This can leave the external calendar permanently out of sync with the DB attendees list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built from the requester's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the organizer's credentials, so when an attendee calls the endpoint the calendar guest list is silently never updated

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the mutation is callable by an attendee (`isAttendee` check allows it). But the calendar update is performed via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...] })`, where `user` is the requester (`ctx.user`), not the booking organizer (`booking.userId` / `organizer`). If an attendee triggers this endpoint, the EventManager will use the attendee’s calendar credentials (often none / not the organizer’s), so `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is very likely to update the wrong account or not update the organizer’s external calendar at all. This is a concrete correctness issue introduced by the diff (caller identity vs organizer identity mismatch).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale validation error persists across dialog reopenings — onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but not isInvalidEmail, showing the red error banner with no invalid input present

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails, but it is only reset to `false` on the Cancel button handler. In the mutation `onSuccess`, the code resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog (`setIsOpenDialog(false)`), but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. Since the dialog component stays mounted inside `BookingListItem`, reopening it will preserve `isInvalidEmail === true` and immediately show the red error banner even though `multiEmailValue` was reset to `[""]` (no new invalid input entered).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error toast construction masks real errors — the template literal is never falsy (rendering 'undefined: ...' when err.data?.code is missing), making the fallback dead code, and t(err.message) assumes all backend messages are translation keys

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the onError handler does `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always produces a string, so `message` is always truthy even when `err.data?.code` is missing (yielding a toast like `"undefined: ..."`). This makes the fallback `t("unable_to_add_guests")` effectively dead code and can mask the intended generic error toast. The additional point that `t(err.message)` assumes the backend message is a translation key is also consistent with this code path (it will try to translate whatever message comes back).

adjudication_records.issue_text: New guests are created with empty names (name: ""), leading to broken greetings like 'Hi ,' and blank names in emails, ICS files, and calendar attendee lists

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, new attendees are created via createMany with `name: ""` for each added guest (`guestsFullDetails`). That means the persisted attendee record has an empty name, and later code builds attendee objects/emails using `attendee.name` (e.g., attendee-add-guests-email.ts sets `to: `${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>``). This can yield blank display names and potentially awkward greetings/headers wherever attendee.name is rendered, so the finding describes a concrete issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled findFirstOrThrow when booking.userId is null (booking.userId || 0 passed as fallback), causing a raw Prisma error and unhandled 500 instead of a typed TRPCError

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 }})`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined` (the code explicitly anticipates this by using `|| 0`), the query becomes `id: 0`, which will not exist and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma exception. That exception is not wrapped in a `TRPCError`, so it will bubble up as an untyped internal error (500) rather than a controlled TRPC error. This is directly verifiable from the diff regardless of how often `userId` is null in practice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic bug: `&&` used instead of `||` in isTeamAdminOrOwner check, requiring caller to be both admin and owner and incorrectly denying team admins who are not owners the ability to manage guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. The variable name and typical permission logic for “admin OR owner” strongly indicate this should be `||`. As written, a team admin who is not also an owner will fail the permission check and be incorrectly denied (`FORBIDDEN`) even though the finding’s intent (admins should manage guests) matches the code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guest email blacklist bypass via case sensitivity: blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` is compared without lowercasing, allowing `Blacklisted@Example.com` to bypass a `blacklisted@example.com` entry
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same case-sensitivity flaw: the blacklist is normalized to lowercase but the input guest email is not, enabling bypass by using uppercase characters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate attendee check `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive, so case-differing duplicate emails slip through

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees via `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. This is a strict, case-sensitive string comparison, and the incoming `guests` values are not normalized (e.g., lowercased) before comparison. Therefore, if an existing attendee email is `test@example.com`, adding `Test@Example.com` will not be detected as a duplicate and can slip through as a “new” guest. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side `.max()` limit or uniqueness refinement on the `guests` array in the schema, allowing duplicate emails within one request to create duplicate attendee rows and send duplicate emails

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (new file) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed via `guests.filter(...)` but that filter only removes emails already in `booking.attendees` or blacklisted; it does not de-duplicate duplicates within the same `guests` array. Therefore a request like `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` can result in duplicate entries in `guestsFullDetails` and `attendees.createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows and then sending duplicate emails because email sending iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` (built from the updated attendees list). The `.max()` part is not evidenced as required, but the uniqueness issue is a real defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side cap or rate limit on number of guest emails an attendee can add, enabling email-bombing / forced information-disclosure of full booking details (description, location, video-call credentials) to arbitrary addresses

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` TRPC mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no max length and no server-side throttling. Any authorized caller (including an existing attendee: `const isAttendee = ...` and permission check allows `isAttendee`) can submit an arbitrarily large list. The handler persists them (`attendees.createMany`) and then sends emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` and updates calendar attendees. The constructed `CalendarEvent` (`evt`) includes `description`, `location`, and `videoCallData` (derived from booking references), so inviting arbitrary addresses can disclose full booking details while also enabling email-bombing by supplying many addresses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses the caller's (ctx.user) credentials in the EventManager instead of the organizer's, causing inconsistency or wrong-calendar mutation when invoked by a non-organizer attendee

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the mutation allows non-organizers (an attendee or team admin/owner) to add guests. However, the calendar mutation is executed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller), not the booking organizer (`booking.userId` / `organizer`). This means `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with the caller’s calendar credentials, which can be incorrect when the caller is not the organizer, potentially mutating the wrong calendar or failing to update the organizer’s calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send errors in sendAddGuestsEmails are silently swallowed — the error object is discarded and the handler still returns success, leaving guests persisted but never notified

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation persists guests via `prisma.booking.update(...)` and updates calendars, then wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` in a `try { ... } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` block. The caught `err` is not logged/returned, and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` even if email sending fails. This can leave guests added but not notified, with no error surfaced to the caller and minimal logging.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation error banner in AddGuestsDialog never clears: setIsInvalidEmail(true) is set on failure but never reset to false, so the error banner persists after the user fixes the input

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd()`, but it is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button handler. It is not reset when the user edits `multiEmailValue`, nor on successful mutation (`onSuccess` resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog but does not call `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). Since the dialog component stays mounted in `BookingListItem`, the error banner can persist even after the user fixes the input (until they cancel/close and reopen or explicitly clear via Cancel).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead fallback in showToast: `message` is always truthy so the `||` fallback branch is unreachable

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`’s `onError`, `message` is built with a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. A template literal always produces a string, and even if `err.data?.code` is `undefined` (or `t(err.message)` returns an empty string), the result is still a non-empty string like `"undefined: "`, which is truthy. Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will always take `message` and the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback branch is effectively unreachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guest input array in addGuests.schema.ts (no .max()) allows unbounded DB writes, email blasts, and calendar API calls — self-service DoS amplification vector

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` with `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` and no `.max()` (or other size limit). This schema is used directly by an authenticated TRPC mutation (`addGuests: authedProcedure.input(ZAddGuestsInputSchema)`), so a client can submit an arbitrarily large `guests` array. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code then (1) builds `guestsFullDetails` for all filtered guests and performs a `createMany` DB write, (2) calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` which can trigger external calendar API work proportional to attendee count, and (3) calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which loops over `calendarEvent.attendees` and sends emails. With no bound, this is a plausible self-service amplification/DoS vector grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be both an admin AND an owner of the team, wrongly rejecting team admins who aren't owners and owners who aren't admins with FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Despite the name implying an OR check, this requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass. This value is then used in the permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`, which will incorrectly forbid a user who is only an admin or only an owner (but not both).

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner queries run even when eventType/teamId is null (passing 0), wasting DB round-trips for every non-team booking

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed unconditionally as:
```ts
(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
(await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
So even when `booking.eventType` is null/undefined or `teamId` is null (non-team booking), both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` are still awaited with `0` as the team id, causing unnecessary DB/query work for those cases. This is directly verifiable from the diff and is a real (performance) defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses ctx.user (the caller's) credentials instead of the organizer's credentials when constructing EventManager, potentially failing or writing to the wrong calendar

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler explicitly allows non-organizers to call the mutation (e.g., an attendee via `isAttendee`). However, when updating the calendar it builds the EventManager with the caller’s identity/credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });` where `user` is `ctx.user`. The organizer is separately fetched as `organizer` (from `booking.userId`), but their credentials are not used. This means if an attendee adds guests, calendar updates (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`) will run under the attendee’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which can reasonably fail or target the wrong connected calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails sends emails to the organizer, every team member, and every existing attendee on each guest-add, not just the new guests, causing O(existing attendees) SMTP sends per mutation
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe that sendAddGuestsEmails operates over the full existing attendee list instead of restricting behavior to the newly added guests, leading to emailing (or at least processing) existing attendees again on each add-guests action. The candidate frames it as excessive/incorrect recipients and O(existing attendees) sends, which is a consequence of the golden issue’s misuse of calendarEvent.attendees vs the newGuests input array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email comparisons defeat the dedupe and blacklist checks (guest not lowercased), allowing blacklist bypass and duplicate attendee rows

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts, blacklist values are normalized to lowercase (`blacklistedGuestEmails = ...map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but incoming `guests` are never lowercased before checks. The filter uses case-sensitive comparisons: `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. This allows bypassing the blacklist by changing email case (e.g., `Blocked@x.com` not matching `blocked@x.com`) and can also defeat dedupe against existing attendees if the same address is provided with different casing, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows (no normalization shown in the diff). The UI-side uniqueness check in AddGuestsDialog (Set on raw strings) is also case-sensitive, reinforcing the issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Original unfiltered guests array (not the filtered uniqueGuests) is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails, causing misclassified email templates and wrong ics status/content for duplicates and blacklisted emails

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the DB update uses `uniqueGuests` (filtered to exclude existing attendees and blacklisted emails), but the email sender is invoked with the original `guests` array: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the provided `newGuests` list to decide per attendee whether to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` via `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))`. If the user submits a mix of emails that includes an already-existing attendee plus at least one truly new guest, `uniqueGuests` will still add the new guest(s), but the existing attendee email remains in `guests`, causing that existing attendee to be misclassified as “new” and receive the wrong template. (Blacklisted emails won’t be in `evt.attendees` so they don’t affect the includes check, and duplicates don’t change `includes` behavior, but the core unfiltered-vs-filtered mismatch is real.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: No transaction or re-check on write allows concurrent addGuests calls for the same email to both pass the dedupe check and insert duplicate attendees

adjudication.rationale: The handler does a read (findFirst include attendees) then filters `guests` against `booking.attendees` and finally writes via `booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` without a transaction/lock. That creates a potential TOCTOU race. However, whether this results in *duplicate* attendees being inserted is not verifiable from the diff: if the underlying attendees table has a unique constraint (e.g., (bookingId,email)), the second concurrent insert would fail rather than create duplicates (and `createMany` here does not use `skipDuplicates`). Since the diff does not show the DB constraints/schema, the claim that duplicates will be inserted is not definitively supported by the shown code changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 throws a raw unhandled Prisma NotFoundError (500) instead of a typed TRPCError when booking.userId is null

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuestsHandler`, the organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined`, this coerces to `0`, and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw Prisma's not-found exception (not a `TRPCError`). There is no try/catch around this call, so the mutation will surface as an internal error instead of a typed/intentional TRPC error. This is a concrete defect in the diff (the `|| 0` pattern explicitly acknowledges the nullable case but handles it incorrectly).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be both team admin and team owner, so plain team admins get FORBIDDEN on team bookings they administer

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Despite the variable name implying “admin OR owner”, the `&&` requires both predicates to be true. As a result, a user who is a team admin but not the team owner will have `isTeamAdminOrOwner === false` and, if they are neither the booking organizer nor an attendee, will hit the `FORBIDDEN` branch. This is a concrete, behavior-affecting permission bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built from the requesting user's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's credentials, causing calendar updates to fail to match stored calendar references or create spurious events when a non-organizer adds guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler explicitly allows non-organizers to add guests (`isAttendee` and intended team admin/owner paths). However, the calendar update is performed with an `EventManager` instantiated from the requesting user (`const { user } = ctx; ... const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials });`). The organizer (and their credentials) are fetched separately (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow(...)`) and even `booking.user` is included with `credentials`, but neither is used to build the `EventManager`. This makes the calendar update depend on the caller's credentials rather than the booking organizer’s, which is a concrete mismatch in the diff and can cause failures/incorrect updates when the caller is an attendee or other non-organizer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarEvent (evt) constructed in the handler never sets the team field, so sendAddGuestsEmails branches on calendarEvent.team?.members find nothing and team members other than the organizer receive no notification emails

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the constructed `evt: CalendarEvent` omits any `team` field (it only sets organizer, attendees, destinationCalendar, etc.). In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, after `formatCalEvent(calEvent)`, it conditionally notifies additional organizers via `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... }`. Since the handler never supplies team/member data to the CalendarEvent (and the booking query also doesn’t include `eventType.team`), this branch will not run, so team members other than the organizer won’t receive the organizer notification emails (unless they happen to be attendees).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email comparison in dedupe and blacklist checks allows blacklisted emails with different casing to bypass the blacklist, duplicate attendees to be inserted, and existing attendees to receive 'new guest' emails

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, dedupe and blacklist checks compare emails case-sensitively: `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. However `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased while `guest` is not, so `Blacklisted@x.com` bypasses a `blacklisted@x.com` entry. Similarly, an existing attendee `test@x.com` will not match an input `Test@x.com`, so it can be treated as “unique” and inserted via `createMany`. Additionally, sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original `guests` array (not normalized) and checks `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so casing differences can cause existing attendees to be misclassified regarding “new guest” handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests input schema is unbounded and permits empty arrays — empty arrays are only rejected after three DB queries with a misleading error code, and no .max() bound allows thousands of guests per request

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.min(1)` and no `.max(n)`, so the schema accepts an empty array and arbitrarily large arrays. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, an empty `guests` array is only rejected later via `if (uniqueGuests.length === 0)` after the handler has already executed multiple DB operations/queries (e.g., `prisma.booking.findFirst`, `isTeamAdmin`/`isTeamOwner` checks, and `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow`). The thrown error uses message `"emails_must_be_unique_valid"`, which is misleading for the empty-array case (not a uniqueness/format issue). Large arrays would proceed to `createMany` and downstream processing without any explicit upper bound.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee-role authorization lets any booking guest (external user with matching email) mutate the organizer's booking and calendar, broadening the trust boundary beyond what the organizer granted

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation is an `authedProcedure` and authorizes the caller if they are a team admin/owner, the organizer (`booking.userId === user.id`), **or an attendee** (`booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)`). This means any authenticated user whose email matches an existing attendee on the booking can call `addGuests` to (1) `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, (2) invoke `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` which updates the organizer’s connected calendars for that booking, and (3) trigger outbound emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails`. That is a real, verifiable trust-boundary expansion introduced by the diff: attendee-role users can mutate the booking and calendar state, not just view it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-send failures are swallowed by a catch block that only does console.log with no error details, so guests exist in DB/calendar but no one is notified and the client still sees a success response

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation performs the DB update and calendar attendee update, then wraps `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails");` and does not log `err`, rethrow, or otherwise signal failure. The handler then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the client mutation will resolve successfully even if email sending fails, and there will be no error detail captured from the exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team permission check uses && instead of || in addGuests.handler.ts, requiring user to be both admin AND owner instead of admin OR owner, denying legitimate team admins

adjudication.rationale:
In addGuests.handler.ts the permission flag is computed as:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

Using `&&` requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner, which is atypical and contradicts the variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. This will deny access to legitimate team admins who are not owners (and vice versa) and can cause an unintended FORBIDDEN error via the subsequent check:

```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN
```

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed with the calling user's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's, causing calendar updates to use wrong or missing credentials when attendees add guests

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, permissions explicitly allow a non-organizer attendee to call the mutation (isAttendee check). However, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller), not the booking organizer (`booking.userId` / `organizer`). This means when an attendee adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run under the attendee's identity/credentials rather than the organizer's, which can lead to updating the wrong calendar or failing due to missing organizer credentials. The diff even loads `booking.user.credentials` but never uses them, reinforcing that this is an introduced correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB write of attendees is not transactional with the calendar update, so a calendar API failure leaves guests persisted in DB without being added to external calendars, showing the user an error despite the change being applied

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB update happens first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and is not wrapped in a transaction with the subsequent external side effect `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (calendar API/network failure), the TRPC mutation will error after the DB write has already committed, leaving new guests persisted in the DB but not synced to external calendars. The client’s `onError` path in `AddGuestsDialog` will then show an error toast even though the DB change was applied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failure is swallowed and the captured err object is never logged, making production debugging impossible and leaving guests silently unnotified

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The caught `err` is not logged (only a generic string is), and the error is swallowed (no rethrow / no user-visible failure), so production debugging loses the exception details and the mutation still returns success even if notifications fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled findFirstOrThrow on organizer lookup throws raw Prisma NotFoundError when booking.userId is null, resulting in an unhelpful INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a proper TRPCError

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } ... })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined` (the code explicitly anticipates this by using `|| 0`), the query runs with `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma NotFoundError. This error is not caught and not converted to a `TRPCError`, so it would surface as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR rather than a clear domain/TRPC error. The issue is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update and CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST email run without checking booking state, so cancelled or past bookings trigger confirmed invites for dead events

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`) fetches the booking and proceeds to (1) update the calendar via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and (2) send emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` without any check on booking state (e.g., cancelled/rejected status) or temporal validity (already ended). The newly added email templates generate ICS payloads with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` (`packages/emails/templates/*add-guests-email.ts`), so invoking this mutation on a cancelled or past booking would still send confirmed invite updates for an event that may be effectively dead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests input instead of uniqueGuests, causing filtered-out existing attendees to receive duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail re-confirmations

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server filters the submitted `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted) and only creates attendees from `uniqueGuests`. However, it then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input, not `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide which template to send; if an existing attendee email was included in the raw input (and thus filtered out from `uniqueGuests`), that attendee will still match and receive an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` re-confirmation instead of the intended add-guests notification, causing unintended duplicate/incorrect emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email comparison in attendee dedupe check (guest === attendee.email) fails to match differently-cased emails, creating duplicate attendee rows and double invites; client-side Set dedupe is also case-sensitive

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the dedupe check uses strict equality `guest === attendee.email` when filtering `uniqueGuests`, with no normalization (`toLowerCase()`), so `Foo@bar.com` and `foo@bar.com` won’t be considered duplicates and can create duplicate attendee rows. The client-side uniqueness check in AddGuestsDialog also uses `new Set(emails)` which is case-sensitive, so it doesn’t prevent differently-cased duplicates either. This can lead to duplicate invites/attendees, and later `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in sendAddGuestsEmails is also case-sensitive, potentially misclassifying which attendees are “new”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation error in AddGuestsDialog is set but never cleared on retry or dialog reopen, leaving stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner and dirty state after successful mutation

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse` fails, but it is only cleared in the Cancel button handler. It is not cleared on successful validation/mutation (`onSuccess` closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but never calls `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). Since the dialog component remains mounted in `BookingListItem` (it’s always rendered and toggled via `open`), reopening the dialog after a prior validation failure can show a stale "Emails must be unique and valid" banner even after a successful add or after reopening without cancelling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests created with empty name: "" which produces malformed recipient headers in AttendeeScheduledEmail (" <email>") and nameless ICS attendees, needing a fallback like email local part

Authorization logic bug in addGuests.handler.ts:49-51: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be both admin and owner, denying team admins who aren't owners with you_do_not_have_permission

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires a user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and the subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, this will incorrectly reject users who are team admins but not owners (and also owners but not admins), resulting in an unwarranted `FORBIDDEN` error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation schema duplicated between client (AddGuestsDialog.tsx) and server (addGuests.schema.ts), and they've diverged: client enforces within-array uniqueness but server doesn't, allowing duplicate attendees to be created via API

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate validation schemas: in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the client defines `ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` enforcing uniqueness within the array, while the server’s `addGuests.schema.ts` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails; it does not deduplicate duplicates within the provided `guests` array. As a result, calling the TRPC `viewer.bookings.addGuests` endpoint directly with duplicate emails can produce duplicate entries passed to `attendees.createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendees (absent an unseen DB uniqueness constraint). This is a concrete divergence and correctness issue present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client Zod schema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is re-instantiated on every render since it's declared inside the component body

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `const ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(...).refine(...)` is indeed declared inside the `AddGuestsDialog` component, so it will be re-created on every render. However, this is a minor performance/memoization nit rather than a clear bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff. The code will still behave correctly; moving it outside the component would be an optimization, not a required fix.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist email comparison in addGuests.handler.ts is case-sensitive against a lowercased list, so 'User@Example.com' bypasses a blacklisted 'user@example.com'; email comparisons should normalize case first

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is split and lowercased (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the check uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where `guest` comes directly from input and is not normalized. Since `includes` is case-sensitive, a differently-cased email (e.g., `User@Example.com`) would not match a blacklisted `user@example.com` and would pass the filter. The same case-sensitivity applies to the existing-attendee duplicate check (`guest === attendee.email`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Errors silently swallowed in addGuests.handler.ts:170-173 with a console.log that discards caught err object, making email failures undiagnosable in production; should use app logger with error and bookingId context

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email-sending block is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The caught `err` is discarded (not logged or rethrown), so if email delivery fails there is no error detail or context (e.g., bookingId/user) to diagnose the failure, and the handler still returns success. This is directly verifiable in the diff and is a real observability/diagnosability defect introduced by the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded English string 'Remove email' in MultiEmail.tsx breaks i18n in an otherwise-localized component now exported from @calcom/ui for app-wide reuse

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the new reusable `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the tooltip text is hardcoded as `content="Remove email"` while the component otherwise uses `useLocale().t(...)` for labels (e.g., `add_another`). This introduces an untranslated English string in a localized UI component exported from `@calcom/ui`, which is a concrete i18n defect visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail in @calcom/ui imports useLocale from @calcom/lib, leaking the package boundary and creating a ui→lib dependency edge that blocks future extraction of the UI package

adjudication.rationale: The new file `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` explicitly imports `useLocale` from `@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale`, which introduces (or reinforces) a direct `@calcom/ui` → `@calcom/lib` dependency edge in the UI package. This is verifiable in the diff. The claim about "blocking future extraction" is forward-looking, but the underlying boundary leak/dependency is real in the introduced code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmailLazy is a copy-paste of PhoneInputLazy with misleading '40kb' comment and lossy double cast ('as unknown as') that erases type checking; the lazy wrapper buys nothing for a tiny component

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `MultiEmailLazy.tsx` using `next/dynamic` with a double cast (`as unknown as typeof import("./MultiEmail").default`) and a copied comment about “40kb”. While the cast does weaken TypeScript type checking and the comment may be inaccurate, neither is a clear, verifiable correctness/security defect introduced by the diff. The claim that the wrapper “buys nothing for a tiny component” and that the 40kb figure is misleading is speculative (size/benefit not evidenced in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale error state in AddGuestsDialog: isInvalidEmail is never cleared when the user edits input, so the error banner stays visible even after input becomes valid; should be derived from or cleared by changes to multiEmailValue and reset on dialog reopen

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` only when `handleAdd` fails Zod validation, but it is not cleared when the user edits `multiEmailValue` (the `MultiEmail` component updates `multiEmailValue` via `setMultiEmailValue` only). The banner is rendered purely from `isInvalidEmail`, so it will remain visible even after inputs become valid until the user clicks Cancel (which resets it) or a successful mutation occurs (which also resets it). Additionally, closing the dialog via `onOpenChange` (e.g., clicking outside) only toggles `isOpenDialog` and does not reset `isInvalidEmail`, so reopening can show a stale error state. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Handler passes raw guests to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of filtered uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees whose emails were redundantly typed to receive the full 'booking scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notification

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler correctly computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted). However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the original `guests` array, not `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` decides which email template to send per attendee via `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) { AttendeeScheduledEmail } else { AttendeeAddGuestsEmail }`. Therefore, if the requester redundantly includes an existing attendee email in the input `guests` alongside at least one truly new guest, that existing attendee’s email will be present in `newGuests` and they will incorrectly receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (the “booking scheduled” email) instead of the “guests added” notification. This is directly implied by the diff and is a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Two near-identical 'add email' buttons inside MultiEmail (value.length branch and empty-state branch) with same icon and onClick but differing testids/labels/styling, creating drift risk; should be consolidated into one handler/button

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, there are two different buttons: when `value.length` is truthy it renders an "add another" button (label `t("add_another")`, testid `add-another-email`) to append another empty field; when `value.length` is falsy it renders an initial "add emails" button (label is the `label` prop, testid `add-emails`) to create the first field. While both push an empty string into the array, they serve distinct UI states and intentionally differ in label/testid/styling. This is not a verifiable bug or defect introduced by the diff—it's at most a maintainability/style suggestion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 174-line addGuests handler mixes four concerns (permission checks, dedup, Prisma update, CalendarEvent construction, calendar syncing, email dispatch) with CalendarEvent assembly block duplicated near-verbatim from editLocation.handler/confirm.handler; should extract shared buildCalendarEventFromBooking(booking) helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `addGuests.handler.ts` is fairly long and performs multiple steps (permission checks, filtering guests, Prisma update, constructing a `CalendarEvent`, syncing via `EventManager`, and sending emails). However, the proposed finding’s core claim—“CalendarEvent assembly block duplicated near-verbatim from editLocation.handler/confirm.handler” and that a shared `buildCalendarEventFromBooking(booking)` should be extracted—cannot be verified from this diff because the referenced handlers are not shown for comparison. The rest is primarily a maintainability/refactoring suggestion rather than a clear defect (bug/security/correctness issue) introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team permission check uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner, requiring the user to be both admin and owner and incorrectly rejecting team admins who are not owners

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and the subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, a team admin who is not also an owner (and not the booking organizer/attendee) would be incorrectly denied. Using `||` would match the intended “admin OR owner” semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email comparisons defeat the blacklist check (blacklisted emails are lowercased but guest emails are not) and duplicate attendee check (=== instead of case-insensitive comparison), allowing bypass via email casing

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the check uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so a blacklisted email can bypass via casing differences (e.g., `Bad@Example.com`). Similarly, the existing-attendee duplicate prevention uses a case-sensitive comparison `guest === attendee.email`, allowing the same mailbox to be added again with different casing. The schema does not enforce normalization, so this is a real correctness/security gap introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side zod schema for guests lacks uniqueness validation and max length, allowing direct API calls with duplicate emails in the array to insert duplicate attendee rows (client-side refinement is not sufficient)
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: duplicate emails in the incoming guests array are not deduplicated/validated for uniqueness server-side, so createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows when the client submits repeated emails. Candidate adds extra notes (max length, client-side refinement) but the core issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cap on the number of guests added, no check against seatsPerTimeSlot or booking size, enabling email-bombing/abuse via mass attendee insertion and N×M email fan-out on repeated calls

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` and then inserts `uniqueGuests` via `createMany` with no upper bound on array size and no rate limiting. There is also no enforcement against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` / seat capacity before adding attendees (those fields are only copied into the `CalendarEvent` later, not validated). After insertion it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which sends emails to organizer + team members + every attendee (`calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`), so repeated calls can cause large email fan-out. This is directly observable from the diff and is not mitigated within the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed from the requester's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, so updateCalendarAttendees may silently no-op or error when called by a non-organizer

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, but `EventManager` is instantiated with the **requesting** user (`const { user } = ctx; ... new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...(await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user))] })`). The booking’s organizer is separately loaded (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId } ... })`) but their credentials are never used. Since the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to add guests (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner), this means a non-organizer caller will attempt to update the organizer’s calendar using the caller’s credentials, which can reasonably fail or no-op because the caller likely lacks the organizer’s calendar integration credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race condition: duplicate check and createMany are not atomic and there is no unique constraint on bookingId + email, so concurrent requests can insert duplicate attendees

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuestsHandler`, the code reads the booking and its current `attendees`, then later does `prisma.booking.update({ attendees: { createMany: ... }})` based on that earlier snapshot. That read-then-write pattern is non-atomic, so concurrent `addGuests` calls could both decide an email is “not yet an attendee” and attempt to insert it.

However, the finding’s key claim (“there is no unique constraint on bookingId + email, so concurrent requests can insert duplicate attendees”) is not fully verifiable from the diff: the Prisma/DB schema (where a unique constraint would be defined) is not shown. If such a constraint exists, the race would more likely cause a constraint violation rather than silent duplicate rows.

So while a TOCTOU-style concurrency issue is plausible from the diff, the specific assertion about duplicate insertion due to *no* unique constraint is speculative based on the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update runs after the DB write and outside any try/catch, so a calendar failure returns an error despite guests being persisted with no rollback; email sending failures are silently swallowed with console.log

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... createMany ...)` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding try/catch and no DB transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (calendar/provider failure), the mutation will error after guests are already stored in the DB, with no rollback path in this diff. Separately, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch { console.log(...) }`, which explicitly swallows failures and only logs, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking status or end-time check, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings, which sends CONFIRMED ICS attachments for cancelled events and re-triggers calendar writes

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts), the code fetches the booking and unconditionally updates attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. There is no check on booking state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) nor any time-based guard (e.g., `endTime` in the past) before performing calendar writes and sending emails. Additionally, the newly added email templates generate ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`packages/emails/templates/*add-guests-email.ts`), so this flow can produce CONFIRMED ICS for bookings that may actually be cancelled/rejected/past.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee permission creates an escalation chain where guests become attendees who can recursively add more guests without organizer involvement

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the authorization explicitly allows any existing attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and it permits the mutation if `isAttendee` is true (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`). The handler then persists the provided `guests` as new `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. Those newly added guests will now satisfy `isAttendee` on subsequent calls (they are in `booking.attendees`), so they can call `addGuests` themselves and add more guests, enabling a recursive escalation chain without organizer/admin involvement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New-guest emails have a malformed To: header with an empty display name (guests created with name: ""), which some SMTP relays reject

adjudication.rationale: The diff does create new guest attendees with `name: ""` (in `addGuests.handler.ts`). The attendee add-guests email builds the To header as ``${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>`` (in `attendee-add-guests-email.ts`), which for an empty name becomes ` <email>`. However, an empty display-name is not inherently malformed: the RFC mailbox `name-addr` allows the display-name to be omitted entirely, and `<email>` (even with leading whitespace) is generally accepted by mail libraries/SMTP servers. The claim that this is a definite, verifiable defect (“some SMTP relays reject”) is speculative and not demonstrably a real bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw guests input instead of uniqueGuests, so filtered-out duplicate/blacklisted emails cause existing attendees to be misclassified as new and resent the full AttendeeScheduledEmail

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server filters the requested guest emails into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only creates attendees from `uniqueGuests`. However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw input `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` decides which template to send per attendee by checking `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` (sending `AttendeeScheduledEmail` in that case). If the caller passed an email that was already an attendee (and thus filtered out from `uniqueGuests` and not newly added), that existing attendee’s email is still present in `guests`, causing `includes(...)` to be true and the existing attendee to be treated as “new” and sent the wrong email/template. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with booking.userId || 0 throws an unhandled 500 error for bookings with null userId instead of a typed TRPCError

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, the organizer is loaded with `await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } ... })`. The handler already treats `booking.userId` as potentially falsy (e.g., `booking.userId || 0`, and `isOrganizer = booking.userId === user.id`), so for a booking where `userId` is `null/undefined`, this will query `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma "not found" exception. That exception is not converted to a `TRPCError` (unlike earlier `booking_not_found`), so it will surface as an internal/untyped error (likely a 500) instead of a typed TRPC error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog state only resets on Cancel and mutation success, so closing via X/Esc/backdrop leaves stale multiEmailValue; the React key={index} on the removable email list is fragile on mid-list removal

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `AddGuestsDialog`, the only places that reset `multiEmailValue` / `isInvalidEmail` are the Cancel button handler and `addGuestsMutation.onSuccess`. But the dialog can also be closed via `Dialog`’s built-in close mechanisms (X button, ESC, backdrop) because it uses `open={isOpenDialog}` and `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`. Those paths will set `isOpenDialog` to false without clearing `multiEmailValue` or `isInvalidEmail`, so reopening the dialog will show stale emails/error state. Separately, `MultiEmail` renders a mutable/removable list with `key={index}`; since items can be removed via `splice(index, 1)`, using the index key can cause React to reuse component instances for different rows after a mid-list removal, which is a known source of incorrect UI/state association (especially if `EmailField` has internal state/validation).
